submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane. bugs_open/477's THIRD surface, found by the bugs_open/477 lane and handed to this lane because it lands on config this lane owns.
rationale:
The delivery email told its recipient we would remind them, and nothing in this estate sends a reminder.

THE CLAUSE, read at the live agent row rather than from seed 651: `WHEN YOU HAVE MOVED / Once your site is off our hosting, press the button here so we stop reminding you: / {{confirm_link}}`. [MEASURED 2026-09-04] one agent can send mail at all, ZERO scheduled tasks target it, one Go action can send mail, and `sites.transfer_confirmed_at` — the column the button writes — has no reader outside the file that writes it.

WHY THIS SURFACE AND NOT THE OTHER TWO. bugs_open/477 measured two surfaces, both Go string literals in renderConfirm, and the 477 lane has corrected those (76ec663d3, inert until a core-manager roll). This third one is worse and cheaper at the same time. Worse: the pages are hypothetical until somebody clicks, whereas this was SENT — the only delivery this estate has ever made (idea.uk, 2026-09-03 19:30:31Z) carried it to a real inbox. Cheaper: the copy is CONFIG by deliberate design (send_delivery_email_action.go:8 states it as a property — 'No copy. The template lives in the STEP CONFIG (DB, owner-editable)'), so it is live on apply with no image and no roll.

REWORDED, NOT DELETED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE. The 477 lane deleted the clause from the two pages, which worked there because those sentences stated the reason to press separately ('Pressing the button below tells us you have moved everything across'). The email's sentence had ONLY the false clause as its reason, so deleting it leaves 'press the button here:' with no answer to why. It now reads 'press the button here to tell us you have moved' — which is what ConfirmTransfer actually does — worded to match the 477 lane's page so the letter and the page it links to say the same thing in the same voice.

THE PARAGRAPH STAYS ON PURPOSE. 'so we stop reminding you' is a better reason to press than mine and it becomes TRUE the moment the 477 lane's follow-up sender ships. Both the migration header and its ROLLBACK say so, and the ROLLBACK additionally refuses to be the route: it tells the reader to write a forward migration recording the clause becoming true, rather than an undo that reads as a mistake being reversed.

APPLIED BEFORE SUBMISSION, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN HIDDEN. debug_historian objected to exactly this on my migration 751 yesterday and the objection was fair. My reason here is different and I am putting it up to be judged, not excused: the live text was a false statement to customers on a config surface with no roll between it and them, so the alternative was leaving an untruth live for the length of a review. The mitigations the 751 round said it could not see are all present and listed as edits: snapshot table, anchor guard that ABORTS on a moved line, DO/RAISE verify, and a committed ROLLBACK.

plan.summary: One clause in delivery-email-sender's body_template: 'press the button here so we stop reminding you' becomes 'press the button here to tell us you have moved'. Anchored on the verbatim line, aborting if it has moved, with a verify that proves exactly one clause changed by arithmetic.

edits.rationale: Exact-literal replace, not a rewrite of the template. The anchor guard aborts if the line is absent, so a concurrent edit by the 477 lane (who offered to ship this themselves) would have refused rather than clobbered — they and I agreed the ordering by message first, and this is the belt to that braces. Guard also asserts exactly one live non-snapshot row, against the duplicate-active-row landmine.

Listed as an edit, which is what my 751 submission failed to do and drew a fair objection for. It restores a FALSE statement, so its header says so and tells the reader not to use it as the route for restoring the stronger wording once the follow-up sender ships — that should be a forward migration recording the clause becoming true.

The rehearsal send is logged with its inputs: orchestration 35849b32 recorded {"to":"aaa@…","sent":true,"zip_link":true}, so a real recipient holds this text.

send_delivery_email_action.go:8 states the copy is config by design; :131 and :173 refuse to send when the template names a placeholder whose link was not produced — which is why the verify asserts {{confirm_link}}, {{zip_link}} and {{live_site}} all survive.

The verify asserts the length delta equals length(new literal) - length(old literal). Anything else means more than one clause changed — stronger than asserting the new text is present, which passes even if a paragraph elsewhere was mangled.
